<!-- pr-reviewer: 6bd49fd926b93d7c238fc791493e127bf776b72b -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge, after #1527.** This PR is stacked on #1527. I reviewed only the commit after `8d5cbe8b` (`6bd49fd9`). #1527 must merge first. Its head has since moved to `40f461fe` (rework), so this branch takes a `git merge origin/main` and a quick re-gate once #1527 lands.

### What looks good
- There is one routing rule. `State::post_options_target` (`crates/ui/src/state_setup_post_options.rs:40`) returns the owner, else #1527's `shared_mount_target`. `route_post_options` (:46) is the only place the options are written from the shell. All five widget routes reach it: Skip pauses and homes (`state.rs` `SetSkipStops`), Output (`state_per_op.rs:19`), and Threading, Smoothing and End units (all three through `SetPostOptions`, `state.rs:3031`). Each one builds `next` from `posting::post_options` (the active setup's options in force). So the setup's new own copy is "what it posts with now, plus the one change", and nothing else it posts with moves.
- Undo uses the existing `SetSetupPostOptions` command. No new command type and no ad hoc field writes.
- The page line can only describe the active setup's page: `setup_pages.rs` `editable()` makes a non-active setup's Post page read-only. So `post_options_target() == Some(name)` always names the setup the widgets would write.
- The old pin was updated for the right reason. In `setup_post_options::the_option_switches_land_on_the_active_setups_own_options`, Setup2 already owned its options at the changed step, so the old assertion was not a two-setup bleed today. It did assert that a setup's page writes the document's options while another setup exists, and any setup created later inherits that. That is exactly the law #1515 and #1526 replace (the decision file's first "dropped" item). The new step also adds a check that undo clears Setup1's own options.
- The decision file states the trade-off: a whole-program post now refuses by name when setups disagree on Output or Threading, where before it silently changed both.
- No unwrap/expect/panic outside tests. Provenance lines are updated. Files are well under 400 lines (`egui_app/tests.rs`, already ~5.2k lines, gains one `mod` line; noted only). No PNG, CHANGELOG, PROCESS_VERSION, build.rs, `.github` or dependency changes. Body has `Changelog:` and ends `Fixes #1526`. Conventional subject.

### Local results (trial-merged with upstream main `41cd9c2c`, clean merge)
| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --no-run` | built |
| app `setup_post_options` | 10 passed |
| app `setup_mounts_post` | 8 passed |
| app `posting` | 17 passed |
| app `project_roundtrip` | 73 passed |
| app `commands_undo` | 30 passed |
| ui lib, single-threaded (`--test-threads=1`, CWD `crates/ui`) | 721 passed, 5 ignored |
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (ui lib + 11 ui suites) | green, 830 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets --no-deps -- -D warnings` | clean |

**Behaviour check (local throwaway test, not pushed).** I used 3 setups, each with a generated face that has a program stop, all driven through `State`:
- Skip on Setup2 (following the document): Setup2 gets its own options. Setup1, Setup3 and the document are unchanged. The posted stream drops exactly one `AfterOperation` (3 to 2), and the whole program still posts.
- Setup3 owns its options and switches Threading to G76. The whole-program post refuses with: `post blocked - setup 'Setup1' posts with other post options (output or threading) than the active setup 'Setup3' - post the setups one at a time; setup 'Setup2' ...`
- Output = one file per operation on Setup1 only: Setup2 and Setup3 are unchanged. Posting refuses by name in the same way, listing Setup2 and Setup3.
- `project::save` then `project::load` into a fresh world: each setup's own and in-force options, and the document's options, round-trip exactly.
- Undo walks every edit back to the document defaults.

**Mutations** (each reverted; scope: the ui `setup_post_options*` tests). None survived:
| Mutation | Killed by |
|---|---|
| target = owner only (old law) | 4 tests |
| target = active setup always (one-setup binds own) | 3 |
| route reads `post_options_owner` while the page reads the target | 4 |
| page line always "own" | 1 |
| page line always "document's" | 1 |
| page line removed | 2 |
| `shared_mount_target` threshold `> 1` changed to `> 2` | 4 |

### Requested before merge
None.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. **End units in a whole-program post.** `program_problems` (`crates/app/src/setup_post_options.rs:85`) refuses a disagreement on Output or Threading only. End units goes into the program from the active setup's options (`posting::options_value`, via `post_options`), so a whole program posts with whichever setup is active. That was already true for setups with their own options. This PR makes the case reachable by default, from one click on Setup2's page. It is controller state after M30, not a cut, so it is not a blocker here. A follow-up should either add End units to `program_problems` or state that the active setup's choice wins.
2. **Wording on the page.** The existing weak note under the radios (`setup_post_page.rs:28-31`) still says "Skip pauses and homes, Output and Threading above are the document's, shared by every setup that follows it." With two or more setups, the new line just below it says an edit becomes this setup's own. Both are true: one describes the values shown, the other where an edit lands. Read together they may confuse. The note also lists 3 of the 5 options (Smoothing and End units route the same way).
3. No 3-setup pin in the PR. The 2-setup pins kill the threshold mutation, and my local 3-setup check passed, so this is optional.
4. The page gains one text line, so a release-lane snapshot golden may move at the cut, as the PR body says.

This merges only after #1527.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
